title: Observable-indexed recovery with gauge-copy erasure
decisive_next_test: Define and bound observable-indexed recovery errors for one real regulated Yang--Mills block map.

target_theorem.name: One-block quotient-observable recovery theorem
requires: explicit fine and retained configuration spaces
typed fine and retained gauge actions
real block map and explicit reconstruction rule
separating normed class of gauge-invariant observables
volume, boundary, cutoff, and retained-history uniform constants

internal_implications.condition: observable class closes under transport and amplification constants remain uniform
block map is invariant, or exactly invariant in the declared quotient metric

internal_implications.from: uniform class error tending to zero
internal_implications.to: continuum recovery for the declared observable class
internal_implications.condition: fixed physical support and complexity, with uniform volume and retained-history control

cross_hypothesis_dependencies.role: typed composition-defect calculus and composition bounds
cross_hypothesis_dependencies.needed_for: stable iteration of one-block recovery estimates

cross_hypothesis_dependencies.role: density and uniform temporal decay after continuum reconstruction
cross_hypothesis_dependencies.needed_for: any spectral or Hilbert-space consequence beyond the recovered core

cross_hypothesis_dependencies.role: OS-compatible physical-length cocycle with uniform errors

cross_hypothesis_dependencies.needed_for: embedding H10 representation control in the primary physical construction

counterexample_obligations: finite probe agreement without observable-algebra recovery
gauge-copy erasure with collapse of physically distinct orbits
invariant-observable recovery while retaining gauge-copy labels
finite-volume convergence without a uniform volume or depth bound
recovery on a non-dense temporal core

not_implied: density of the recovered observable core
